## Fix landed for review — Gerrit 1992

**Current message, as observed firing** (not read from source): dropped a throwaway test that
writes a top-level file into this worktree's REPO_ROOT, ran pytest, exit status 1:

    REPO ISOLATION FAILURE: the test run left new changes in the checkout (a test wrote
    into the working tree instead of tmp_path). Offending entries from `git status
    --porcelain`:
      ?? BLUEJAY_PROBE.txt

**New message, same probe, same exit status 1:**

    REPO ISOLATION FAILURE: new changes appeared in the checkout during this test run.
    Entries from `git status --porcelain`:
      ?? BLUEJAY_PROBE.txt
    The backstop only diffs `git status --porcelain` around the whole session, so it
    cannot tell which process wrote them.
    If a test wrote them, sandbox it — write under tmp_path (or another disposable temp
    dir) instead of the checkout.
    If none did, a concurrent write from outside the suite looks identical here: a
    detached run shares this checkout with whatever else is committing, building, or
    saving in it.

It conditions on what only the reader can know, in the same two-branch shape
`leak_failure_message` uses, and drops "Offending" — which presumed wrongdoing before the
cause was established. No detection signal was invented; agreeing with both siblings, none
exists for two porcelain samples.

**Detection is unchanged, and now pinned.** The backstop fires on the same condition, names
every entry, and still sets `session.exitstatus = TESTS_FAILED`. A new end-to-end test drives
the REAL `pytest_sessionfinish` against a disposable repo (same hand-driven shape the sibling
guards' tests use) and asserts that escalation. Seeding a detection break — deleting the
`session.exitstatus` line — turns it RED, so the pin has teeth.

**RED to GREEN.** The message was first extracted into `tests/_isolation.py` verbatim, and the
message was verified byte-identical through the observed probe before any wording changed —
so the wording fix is a real RED, not an import error. Both new wording tests then failed on
the live text, the fix was written by a subagent that never saw them (the test files were
moved out of its tree and declared off-limits), and both went GREEN. Restoring the old wording
returns both to RED; restoring the fix returns them to GREEN.

**Gates.** `make lint` (ruff check + format-check, complexity ratchet `new=0 increased=0
stale=0`, config/env/DCO/criteria/frontmatter gates, zizmor, actionlint) and `make typecheck`
both pass. Full unit sweep: **11992 passed, 44 skipped, exit 0** — including the repo-wide
oracles the fast gates skip.

**No test was weakened.** The only removed line in either test file is a one-line import
replaced by its multi-line form; every pre-existing assertion is untouched.

**Sibling sweep.** Construct axis: the family is complete at three. The only other live
"a test did X" strings are the `_INLINE_CONFTEST` pytester fixture in
`test_repo_isolation_guard.py` (a throwaway repo with no concurrent writer, where the
attribution is actually true) and static-analysis findings in `test_ruff_ratchet.py` /
`test_ci_actionlint_scope.py`, which identify the offending artifact deterministically. Parity
axis: the rule is "a shared-checkout state guard's failure text must not assert which process
changed the state". No CLI, MCP, or library surface performs this operation — the only callers
of the `tests/_isolation.py` core are the three conftest guards, all three now compliant. The
mirror direction (a guard reporting state *disappearing*) does not exist.

**Residual.** `docs/local-dev-env.md` lists the two per-test guards among those that misfire on
a concurrent writer, but not this session backstop. Filed as `beamy-glacial-waterbuck`, linked
`discovered_from` this bug.

**Origin.** `caused_by` -> `gusto-pixel-signal` (`4c79-3873-807d-4a0d`), the commit that
authored this message. Same origin the sibling `hot-guessable-ungulate` recorded; close class
will be `plan_defect`.
